He showed promise as a leader even before he assumed full authority.

He sought alliances with the Kingdom of Jerusalem and the County of Tripoli's vassals. He also engaged in diplomacy with Muslim leaders such as Nur ad-Din and Saladin. He participated in several military campaigns against Muslim forces. He fought at the Battle of Harim in 1164. He suffered a defeat but managed to escape capture. He later negotiated treaties that allowed for temporary peace. He faced internal strife when some nobles challenged his authority. He quelled rebellions with decisive action. He also dealt with the rise of the Assassins who threatened the region. His reign saw both periods of war and uneasy truces.
